claims.text: The Co-free alloy is FeNiCrMn derived by removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The initial Co-free alloy has an as-solidified, single-phase solid-solution microstructure.
Dynamic behavior is controlled by a transition from dislocation slip to deformation twinning.
Removing Co changes the stacking-fault energy of the alloy.
A Co-related change in stacking-fault energy alters the stress threshold for activating deformation twinning.
Local stacking-fault-energy variations govern the relative ease of dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
At lower temperatures, the altered stacking-fault energy in Co-free FeNiCrMn promotes earlier twinning relative to dislocation slip.
At higher strain rates, the altered stacking-fault energy in Co-free FeNiCrMn promotes earlier twinning relative to dislocation slip.
The resulting change in deformation mechanism modifies the strength–ductility balance under dynamic conditions.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will exhibit a shifted transition point between slip-dominated and twin-dominated deformation.
At critical temperature–strain-rate combinations, Co-free FeNiCrMn will exhibit enhanced twin formation relative to the baseline alloy.
At critical temperature–strain-rate combinations, Co-free FeNiCrMn will exhibit an altered yield response relative to the baseline alloy.
The proposed mechanism is limited to as-solidified, single-phase material in regimes where slip and twinning compete.
The proposed behavior may not apply to heavily processed or thermally aged material.
